title.en: Volume 124 Biographies 49: Yao Cong, Song Jing
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 列傳第四十九 姚崇 宋璟 Volume 124 Biographies 49: Yao Cong, Song Jing

sentences.zh: 姚崇，字元之，陝州硤石人。

translations.literal: Yao Chong, styled Yuanzhi, was a native of Xiashi in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhi, came from Xiashi in Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父懿，字善懿，貞觀中，為巂州都督，贈幽州大都督，諡文獻。

translations.literal: His father Yi, styled Shanyi, in the Zhenguan era served as military commissioner of Yi Prefecture, was posthumously made Grand Military Commissioner of You Prefecture, and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao Yi, courtesy name Shanyi, had served as commissioner of Yi Prefecture during the Zhenguan reign and was posthumously honored as Grand Military Commissioner of You Prefecture with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 崇少倜儻，尚氣節，長乃好學。

translations.literal: Chong in youth was unconventional, prized integrity of spirit, and in maturity came to love learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yao Chong was dashing and independent-minded, holding fast to principle; only later did he turn seriously to study.

sentences.zh: 仕為孝敬挽郎，舉下筆成章，授濮州司倉參軍，五遷夏官郎中。

translations.literal: He entered office as a mourning groom for the Prince of Respectful Filiality, was recommended for writing composition at a stroke, was appointed assistant in the granary office of Pu Prefecture, and was transferred five times to become a director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a funeral attendant for the Prince of Respectful Filiality, passed the examination for fluent composition on the spot, was appointed assistant in the granary office of Pu Prefecture, and rose through five promotions to become a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 契丹擾河北，兵檄叢進，崇奏決若流，武后賢之，即拜侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Khitan harassed Hebei, military dispatches piled in; Chong's memorials were decided like flowing water. Empress Wu considered him worthy and immediately appointed him Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided Hebei and military dispatches flooded in, Yao Chong's decisions flowed as swiftly as his drafts. Empress Wu admired his ability and promptly appointed him vice minister.

sentences.zh: 後嘗語左右：「往周興、來俊臣等數治詔獄，朝臣相逮引，一切承反。

translations.literal: The Empress once said to those beside her: "Formerly Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others repeatedly handled imperial prison cases; court officials were implicated one after another, and all confessed to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress once told her attendants, "In the past Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others ran repeated political trials, and court officials were dragged in one after another until everyone confessed to treason.

sentences.zh: 朕意其枉，更畏近臣臨問，皆得其手牒不冤，朕無所疑，即可其奏。

translations.literal: I thought them wronged, yet feared that when close ministers interrogated them, all obtained their written confessions that they were not wronged; I had no doubts and at once approved their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: I suspected they were innocent, but when my close ministers questioned them, every case came back with written confessions and no sign of injustice, so I had no doubts and approved the verdicts at once.

sentences.zh: 自俊臣等誅，遂無反者，然則向論死得無冤邪？」

translations.literal: Since Junchen and the others were executed, there have been no rebels—yet then, were those sentenced to death not wronged?
translations.idiomatic: Since Junchen and his ilk were executed there have been no more rebels—so were all those earlier death sentences free of injustice?

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「自垂拱後，被告者類自誣。

translations.literal: Chong said: "Since the Chui Gong era, the accused mostly falsely incriminated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong replied, "Since the Chui Gong era most defendants ended up falsely incriminating themselves.

sentences.zh: 當是時，以告言為功，故天下號曰'羅織'，甚於漢之鉤黨。

translations.literal: At that time, to lodge accusations was counted as merit, so all under Heaven called it 'fabrication,' worse than the Party Affiliation Cases of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Accusation itself counted as merit then, and the realm called the practice 'fabricating charges,' worse than the partisan prosecutions of Han.

sentences.zh: 雖陛下使近臣覆訊，彼尚不自保，敢一搖手以悖酷吏意哉！

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty sent close ministers to re-examine cases, they still could not protect themselves—how would they dare move a hand against the cruel officials' intent!
translations.idiomatic: Even when Your Majesty sent close ministers to reinvestigate, they could not protect themselves—who would dare lift a finger against the cruel prosecutors' will?

sentences.zh: 且被問不承，則重罹其慘，如張虔勖、李安靜等皆是也。

translations.literal: Moreover, if questioned and one did not confess, one suffered their cruelty anew, as with Zhang Qianxu, Li Anjing, and others—all were thus.
translations.idiomatic: And if a prisoner under interrogation refused to confess, he suffered their cruelty all over again, as Zhang Qianxu and Li Anjing did.

sentences.zh: 今賴天之靈，發寤陛下，凶豎殲夷，朝廷乂安，臣以一門百口保內外官無復反者。

translations.literal: Now, relying on Heaven's spirit, Your Majesty has awakened; the vicious have been destroyed, and the court is at peace. I pledge with the hundred mouths of my household that among inner and outer officials there will be no rebels again.
translations.idiomatic: Now, thanks to Heaven's grace, Your Majesty has awakened, the villains have been destroyed, and the court is at peace. I stake the lives of my entire household on there being no more rebels among officials within or without the palace.

sentences.zh: 陛下以告牒置弗推，後若反有端，臣請坐知而不告。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty sets aside accusation documents without pursuing them, and later if rebellion has any sign, I ask to be punished for knowing and not reporting.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sets aside accusation documents without pursuing them, and rebellion later shows any sign of it, I ask to be punished for knowing and failing to report it.

sentences.zh: 後悅曰：「前宰相務順可，陷我為淫刑主，聞公之言，乃得朕心。」

translations.literal: The Empress said with pleasure: "Former chancellors only sought to please me and trapped me as a master of licentious punishments. Hearing your words, you have won my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said with pleasure, "Former chancellors only sought to please me and made me out to be a tyrant of cruel punishments. Hearing your words, you have won my heart.

sentences.zh: 賜銀千兩。

translations.literal: She bestowed a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: She rewarded him with a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 聖曆三年，進同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenglì he was advanced to Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenglì he was promoted to associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 遷鳳閣侍郎，俄兼相王府長史，以母老納政歸侍，乃詔以相王府長史侍疾，月餘，復兼夏官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion, and soon also served as Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household. Because his mother was old he resigned office to return and attend her; an edict then appointed him Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household to nurse her illness. After more than a month he again concurrently held Minister of War and Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion and soon also served as chief administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household. When his mother grew old he resigned to care for her at home, so an edict named him chief administrator of the prince's household to attend her illness. After a month he again held the post of minister of war with third rank at the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 崇建言：「臣事相王，而夏官本兵，臣非惜死，恐不益王。」

translations.literal: Chong submitted a proposal: "I serve the Prince of Xiang, yet the Ministry of Summer is fundamentally military. It is not that I begrudge death, but I fear it will not benefit the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong submitted a proposal: "I serve the Prince of Xiang, yet the Ministry of War controls the armies. It is not that I begrudge my life, but I fear the post will not benefit the prince.

sentences.zh: 乃詔改春官。

translations.literal: An edict then changed him to the Ministry of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then transferred him to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 張易之私有請於崇，崇不納，易之譖於後，降司僕卿，猶同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi made a private request of Chong; Chong did not accept it. Yizhi slandered him to the Empress, and he was demoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, yet still held Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi made a private request of Yao Chong, who refused. Yizhi slandered him to the Empress, and Chong was demoted to vice director of the imperial stud while retaining third rank at the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 出為靈武道大總管。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Commander of the Lingwu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as grand commander of the Lingwu circuit.

sentences.zh: 張柬之等謀誅二張，崇適自屯所還，遂參計議。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi and others plotted to execute the two Zhangs; Chong happened to return from his garrison post and thus joined in the deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianzhi and others plotted to kill the two Zhang brothers, Yao Chong happened to return from his garrison and joined their deliberations.

sentences.zh: 以功封梁縣侯，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liang County with a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liang County with a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後遷上陽宮，中宗率百官起居，王公更相慶，崇獨流涕。

translations.literal: After the move to Shangyang Palace, Zhongzong led the hundred officials in attendance; princes and dukes congratulated one another, but Chong alone wept.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Shangyang Palace, Emperor Zhongzong led the officials in attendance while princes and dukes congratulated one another; Yao Chong alone wept.

sentences.zh: 柬之等曰：「今豈涕泣時邪？

translations.literal: Jianzhi and the others said: "Is this the time for tears?
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi and the others said, "Is this a time for tears?

sentences.zh: 恐公禍由此始。」

translations.literal: I fear your calamity will begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: I fear your downfall will begin from this.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「比與討逆，不足以語功，然事天后久，違舊主而泣，人臣終節也，由此獲罪甘心焉。」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Compared with suppressing rebellion, this is not enough to speak of merit; yet I served the Heavenly Empress long. To weep against one's former sovereign is a minister's final integrity. If I am punished for this, I accept it gladly."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong said, "Our part in putting down rebellion hardly counts as merit, but I served the Heavenly Empress for many years. To weep for one's former sovereign is a minister's final duty. If I am punished for it, I accept that gladly."

sentences.zh: 俄為亳州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 後五王被害，而崇獨免。

translations.literal: Later the Five Princes were killed, but Chong alone escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Five Princes were killed, Yao Chong alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 曆宋、常、越、許四州。

translations.literal: He served in succession the four prefectures of Song, Chang, Yue, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Song, Chang, Yue, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，進中書令。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was established, he was appointed Minister of War, Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Yao Chong was appointed minister of war and third-rank chancellor, then promoted to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，太平公主干政，宋王成器等分典閑廄、禁兵。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace; Princess Taiping interfered in government, and the Prince of Song Chengqi and others separately controlled the spare stables and the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was crown prince, Princess Taiping meddled in government, and the Prince of Song Chengqi and others separately controlled the spare stables and the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 崇與宋璟建請主就東都，出諸王為刺史，以壹人心。

translations.literal: Chong and Song Jing proposed that the princess go to the Eastern Capital and that the princes be sent out as prefects, in order to unify hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong and Song Jing proposed that the princess retire to the eastern capital and that the princes be sent out as prefects to unify the realm's allegiance.

sentences.zh: 帝以謂主，主怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor reported this to the princess; the princess was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reported the plan to the princess, and she grew furious.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，上疏以崇等槊間王室，請加罪，貶為申州刺史。

translations.literal: The crown prince was afraid and submitted a memorial accusing Chong and the others of driving a wedge into the royal house, asking that they be punished; they were demoted to Prefect of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, fearing for himself, memorialized that Chong and the others were driving a wedge into the royal house and asked that they be punished; Yao Chong was demoted to prefect of Shen.

sentences.zh: 移徐、潞二州，遷揚州長史。

translations.literal: He was moved through the two prefectures of Xu and Lu, then transferred to Chief Administrator of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred through Xu and Lu, then appointed chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 政條簡肅，人為紀德於碑。

translations.literal: His administrative rules were simple and austere; the people recorded his virtue on steles.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was simple and austere, and the people recorded his virtue on stone monuments.

sentences.zh: 徙同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Tong.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，玄宗講武新豐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, Xuanzong reviewed troops at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantian, Emperor Xuanzong held a military review at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 故事，天子行幸，牧守在三百里者，得詣行在。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the Son of Heaven traveled, prefects and defenders within three hundred li might come to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when the emperor traveled, prefects and military commissioners within three hundred li could present themselves at the temporary court.

sentences.zh: 時帝亦密召崇，崇至，帝方獵渭濱，即召見，帝曰：「公知獵乎？」

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor also secretly summoned Chong. When Chong arrived, the Emperor was hunting on the Wei shore and at once received him. The Emperor said: "Do you know hunting?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also secretly summoned Yao Chong. When Chong arrived, the emperor was hunting on the Wei River and received him at once. The emperor asked, "Do you know hunting?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「少所習也。

translations.literal: He replied: "In youth I practiced it somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I practiced it somewhat in my youth.

sentences.zh: 臣年二十，居廣成澤，以呼鷹逐獸為樂。

translations.literal: When I was twenty I lived at Guangcheng Marsh and took my pleasure in calling hawks to chase game.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty I lived at Guangcheng Marsh and took my pleasure in flying hawks after game.

sentences.zh: 張憬藏謂臣當位王佐，無自棄，故折節讀書，遂待罪將相。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingzang told me I ought to stand as a king's assistant and must not abandon myself; therefore I restrained my manner and read books, and thus I await punishment among chancellors and generals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingzang told me I was fit to serve as a king's right hand and must not throw my life away, so I disciplined myself and took up study, and thus I now stand among chancellors and generals awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 然少為獵師，老而猶能。」

translations.literal: Yet though in youth I was a huntsman, in old age I can still do it.
translations.idiomatic: Though I was a huntsman in youth, I can still manage it in old age.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，與俱馳逐，緩速如旨，帝歡甚。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and rode in chase with him; fast and slow were as the Emperor wished, and the Emperor was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rode in chase with him, keeping pace exactly as the emperor wished, and was greatly delighted.

sentences.zh: 既罷，乃咨天下事，袞袞不知倦。

translations.literal: When it was over, he then consulted on affairs of all under Heaven, speaking in an unbroken stream without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: When the hunt ended, he consulted Chong on affairs throughout the realm, talking on and on without weariness.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿宜遂相朕。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You ought at once to serve as my chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You ought to become my chancellor at once.

sentences.zh: 崇知帝大度，銳於治，乃先設事以堅帝意，即陽不謝，帝怪之。

translations.literal: Chong knew the Emperor was magnanimous and keen on governance; he therefore first set forth matters to firm the Emperor's intent, and then openly did not thank him. The Emperor found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor was magnanimous and keen to govern, Yao Chong first laid out certain matters to test his resolve, then openly declined to thank him. The emperor found this strange.

sentences.zh: 崇因跪奏：「臣願以十事聞，陛下度不可行，臣敢辭。」

translations.literal: Chong then knelt and submitted: "I wish to report ten matters. If Your Majesty judges them unfeasible, I dare decline office.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong then knelt and said, "I wish to lay ten matters before you. If Your Majesty judges any of them unfeasible, I dare decline the post.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「試為朕言之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Try to speak them for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Tell me what they are."

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「垂拱以來，以峻法繩下；

translations.literal: Chong said: "Since Chui Gong, harsh law has bound those below;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong said, "Since the Chui Gong era harsh laws have bound those below;

sentences.zh: 臣願政先仁恕，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish that governance put benevolence and forbearance first—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governance put benevolence and forbearance first—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 朝廷覆師青海，未有牽復之悔；

translations.literal: the court lost its army at Qinghai and has had no regret of pulling back;
translations.idiomatic: the court lost its army at Qinghai without repenting of overreach;

sentences.zh: 臣願不倖邊功，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish not to seek frontier merit by chance—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we not chase lucky frontier victories—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 比來壬佞冒觸憲網，皆得以寵自解；

translations.literal: of late crafty flatterers who offended the law have all been able to escape through favor;
translations.idiomatic: of late crafty flatterers who broke the law have all escaped through favor;

sentences.zh: 臣願法行自近，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish the law enforced beginning with those close at hand—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the law be enforced beginning with those close at hand—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 後氏臨朝，喉舌之任出閹人之口；

translations.literal: when the Empress held court, the task of voice and tongue came from eunuchs' mouths;
translations.idiomatic: when the Empress held court, the power of speech came from eunuchs;

sentences.zh: 臣願宦豎不與政，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish palace attendants not to share in government—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that palace eunuchs not share in government—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 戚裏貢獻以自媚於上，公卿方鎮浸亦為之；

translations.literal: imperial kin by marriage presented tribute to flatter those above, and grandees and frontier commissioners gradually did the same;
translations.idiomatic: imperial in-laws sent tribute to curry favor, and grandees and frontier commissioners gradually followed suit;

sentences.zh: 臣願租賦外一絕之，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish all such gifts outside rent and tax abolished at a stroke—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all such gifts beyond rent and tax be abolished at a stroke—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 外戚貴主更相用事，班序荒雜；

translations.literal: consorts' kin and honored princesses used one another in turn in power, and court ranks were chaotic and mixed;
translations.idiomatic: consorts' kin and honored princesses took turns wielding power, and court ranks fell into disorder;

sentences.zh: 臣請戚屬不任台省，可乎？

translations.literal: I ask that imperial kin not hold posts in the central ministries—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that imperial kin not hold posts in the central ministries—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 先朝褻狎大臣，虧君臣之嚴；

translations.literal: the former court treated great ministers with familiarity, impairing the solemnity between ruler and minister;
translations.idiomatic: the former court treated great ministers too familiarly, impairing the dignity between ruler and minister;

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下接之以禮，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to receive them with ritual propriety—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty receive them with proper ritual—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 燕欽融、韋月將以忠被罪，自是諍臣沮折；

translations.literal: Yan Qinrong and Wei Yuejiang were punished for loyalty; from this remonstrating ministers were broken;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qinrong and Wei Yuejiang were punished for loyalty, and remonstrating ministers have been broken ever since;

sentences.zh: 臣願群臣皆得批逆鱗，犯忌諱，可乎？

translations.literal: I wish that all ministers may stroke the dragon's scales against the grain and violate taboos—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all ministers be free to speak against the grain and violate taboo—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 武后造福先寺，上皇造金仙、玉真二觀，費钜百萬；

translations.literal: Empress Wu built blessings at Xian Temple; the Retired Emperor built the two abbeys Jinxian and Yuzhen, costing millions;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu built the Xian Temple at vast expense, and the Retired Emperor built the Jinxian and Yuzhen abbeys, costing millions;

sentences.zh: 臣請絕道佛營造，可乎？

translations.literal: I ask to cut off Daoist and Buddhist construction—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Daoist and Buddhist construction be ended—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 漢以祿、莽、閻、梁亂天下，國家為甚；

translations.literal: Han was thrown into disorder by the Lu, Wang Mang, Yan, and Liang clans—the state suffered especially;
translations.idiomatic: Han was thrown into disorder by the Lu, Wang, Yan, and Liang clans, and our dynasty has suffered even more;

sentences.zh: 臣願推此鑒戒為萬代法，可乎？」

translations.literal: I wish to extend this mirror and warning as law for ten thousand generations—may this be done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this lesson be made law for ten thousand generations—may this be done?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕能行之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I can carry these out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I can carry these out."

sentences.zh: 崇乃頓首謝。

translations.literal: Chong then bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong then bowed his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 翌日，拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed Minister of War and Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was appointed minister of war and third-rank chancellor.

sentences.zh: 封梁國公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 遷紫微令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Purple Forbidden Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 固辭實封，乃停舊食，賜新封百戶。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the substantive fief; his old sustenance was then stopped and a new fief of a hundred households was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the substantive fief, so his old sustenance was stopped and a new fief of a hundred households was granted instead.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，近戚奏度僧尼，溫戶強丁因避賦役。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time, close kin memorialized to ordain monks and nuns; warm households and strong young men thereby avoided rent and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong, imperial in-laws petitioned to ordain monks and nuns, and prosperous households sent strong young men into the clergy to escape taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 至是，崇建言：「佛不在外，悟之於心。

translations.literal: At this time Chong submitted a proposal: "The Buddha is not outside; enlightenment is in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yao Chong submitted a proposal: "The Buddha is not outside us; enlightenment lies in the heart.

sentences.zh: 行事利益，使蒼生安穩，是謂佛理。

translations.literal: To act for benefit and make the black-haired people secure and settled—this is called Buddhist principle.
translations.idiomatic: To act for the common good and keep the people secure and settled—that is Buddhist principle.

sentences.zh: 烏用奸人以汨真教？」

translations.literal: Why use treacherous men to defile the true teaching?
translations.idiomatic: Why let treacherous men defile the true teaching?

sentences.zh: 帝善之，詔天下汰僧偽濫，發而農者余萬二千人。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it and ordered all under Heaven to weed out false and excessive monks; those released to farming numbered more than twelve thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it and ordered the realm to weed out false and excessive clergy; more than twelve thousand who were released returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 崇嘗於帝前序次郎吏，帝左右顧，不主其語。

translations.literal: Chong once before the Emperor ranked the clerks in order; the Emperor looked to left and right and did not attend to his words.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong once ranked the clerks in order before the emperor, but the emperor looked about and paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 崇懼，再三言之，卒不答，崇趨出。

translations.literal: Chong was afraid and spoke them again and again; in the end there was no answer, and Chong hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong grew afraid and repeated himself again and again, but received no answer and hurried out.

sentences.zh: 內侍高力士曰：「陛下新即位，宜與大臣裁可否。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Gao Lishi said: "Your Majesty has newly taken the throne; you ought to decide with great ministers what may or may not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Gao Lishi said, "Your Majesty has newly taken the throne; you ought to decide with your great ministers what may or may not be done.

sentences.zh: 今崇亟言，陛下不應，非虛懷納誨者。」

translations.literal: Now Chong speaks urgently and Your Majesty does not respond—this is not one who with empty bosom receives admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chong speaks urgently and Your Majesty does not respond—that is not the conduct of one who openly receives counsel.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我任崇以政，大事吾當與決，至用郎吏，崇顧不能而重煩我邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I entrust Chong with government; on great affairs I ought to decide with him. As for employing clerks—does Chong look unable and therefore trouble me again?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I entrust Chong with government; on great affairs I decide with him. As for appointing clerks—does he think I cannot handle that and must trouble me again?"

sentences.zh: 崇聞乃安。

translations.literal: When Chong heard this he was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong heard this he was reassured.

sentences.zh: 由是進賢退不肖而天下治。

translations.literal: From this he advanced the worthy and removed the unworthy, and all under Heaven was governed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he advanced the worthy and removed the unworthy, and the realm was well governed.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，山東大蝗，民祭且拜，坐視食苗不敢捕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, Shandong suffered great locusts; the people sacrificed and bowed, sitting and watching them eat the seedlings without daring to catch them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan eastern Shandong suffered a great locust plague; the people sacrificed and bowed to the insects, watching them devour the seedlings without daring to kill them.

sentences.zh: 崇奏：「《詩》云：'秉彼蟊賊，付畀炎火。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized: "The Odes say: 'Take up those injurious pests and deliver them to blazing fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong memorialized, "The Odes say, 'Take up those injurious pests and deliver them to blazing fire.

sentences.zh: '漢光武詔曰：'勉順時政，勸督農桑。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han's edict says: 'Exhort compliance with the season's government and urge supervision of farming and sericulture.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han's edict says, 'Exhort compliance with the season's policies and urge supervision of farming and sericulture.'

sentences.zh: 去彼螟域，以及蟊賊。

translations.literal: Remove those stem-borers and extend to the injurious pests.
translations.idiomatic: Drive off those stem-borers and reach the injurious pests as well.

sentences.zh: '此除蝗誼也。

translations.literal: This is the meaning of eliminating locusts.
translations.idiomatic: This is the very meaning of eliminating locusts.

sentences.zh: 且蝗畏人易驅，又田皆有主，使自救其地，必不憚勸。

translations.literal: Moreover, locusts fear men and are easily driven; moreover every field has an owner—if made to save their own land, they will surely not fear exhortation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, locusts fear people and are easily driven off, and every field has an owner; if people are made to save their own land, they will surely heed encouragement.

sentences.zh: 請夜設火，坎其旁，且焚且瘞，蝗乃可盡。

translations.literal: I ask that fires be set by night with pits beside them; burning and burying together, the locusts can then be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that fires be set by night with pits dug beside them; burning and burying together, the locusts can then be destroyed completely.

sentences.zh: 古有討除不勝者，特人不用命耳。」

translations.literal: In antiquity there were campaigns to eliminate them that did not succeed—only because men did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity campaigns to eliminate them sometimes failed only because people did not obey orders.

sentences.zh: 乃出御史為捕蝗使，分道殺蝗。

translations.literal: Censors were then sent out as locust-capturing commissioners, each on his route to kill locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were then sent out as locust commissioners, each on his own route to kill the pests.

sentences.zh: 汴州刺史倪若水上言：「除天災者當以德，昔劉聰除蝗不克而害愈甚。」

translations.literal: Ni Ruoshui, Prefect of Bian, submitted: "He who removes Heaven's calamities ought to use virtue. Formerly Liu Cong tried to eliminate locusts without success and the harm grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Ruoshui, prefect of Bian, submitted, "He who removes Heaven's calamities ought to rely on virtue. Formerly Liu Cong tried to eliminate locusts without success and the harm grew worse.

sentences.zh: 拒御史不應命。

translations.literal: He declined the censor and did not respond to the order.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui refused the imperial censors and would not comply with the order.

sentences.zh: 崇移書誚之曰：「聰偽主，德不勝祆，今祆不勝德。

translations.literal: Chong sent a letter reproaching him, saying: "Cong was a false ruler; virtue could not overcome the baleful omen—now the baleful omen cannot overcome virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong sent a letter rebuking him: "Liu Cong was a usurper; virtue could not overcome evil omens—yet now evil omens cannot overcome virtue.

sentences.zh: 古者良守，蝗避其境，謂修德可免，彼將無德致然乎？

translations.literal: In antiquity good prefects had locusts avoid their territories—people said cultivating virtue could avert them; will you say they had no virtue and that is why this happened?
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity worthy prefects saw locusts shun their jurisdictions; people held that cultivating virtue could ward them off—will you claim those men lacked virtue and brought this on themselves?

sentences.zh: 今坐視食苗，忍而不救，因以無年，刺史其謂何？」

translations.literal: Now you sit and watch them eat the seedlings, enduring without rescue, thereby bringing on famine—what shall we say of a prefect?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you sit by while they devour the young crops, refusing to act, and thereby invite famine—what is a prefect to be called?

sentences.zh: 若水懼，乃縱捕，得蝗十四萬石。

translations.literal: Ruoshui was afraid and then allowed capture; they obtained one hundred forty thousand piculs of locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Ruoshui at last permitted extermination; one hundred forty thousand piculs of locusts were collected.

sentences.zh: 時議者喧嘩，帝疑，復以問崇，對曰：「庸儒泥文不知變。

translations.literal: At the time the debaters clamored; the Emperor was doubtful and again questioned Chong, who replied: "Mediocre Confucians cling to text and do not know change.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion at court was loud and divided; the emperor hesitated and questioned Chong again. He answered, "Mediocre scholars cling to the letter of the law and do not know how to adapt.

sentences.zh: 事固有違經而合道，反道而適權者。

translations.literal: Affairs indeed have those that violate the classics yet accord with the Way, and those that go against the Way yet suit expediency.
translations.idiomatic: There are matters that breach canonical precedent yet accord with principle, and cases that defy principle yet serve expedient need.

sentences.zh: 昔魏世山東蝗，小忍不除，至人相食；

translations.literal: Formerly in Wei times there were locusts east of the mountains; a little patience in not removing them led to men eating one another;
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times locusts plagued the eastern provinces; because removal was delayed, people eventually ate one another;

sentences.zh: 後奏有蝗，草木皆盡，牛馬至相啖毛。

translations.literal: later when locusts were reported, grass and trees were all consumed, and cattle and horses even came to chew one another's hair.
translations.idiomatic: later, when locusts were again reported, vegetation was stripped bare and cattle and horses gnawed each other's hides.

sentences.zh: 今飛蝗所在充滿，加復蕃息，且河南、河北家無宿藏，一不獲則流離，安危系之。

translations.literal: Now flying locusts fill every place where they are, moreover breeding again; and in Henan and Hebei households have no stored grain—if harvest fails once they become displaced wanderers; safety and danger hang on this.
translations.idiomatic: Flying locusts now swarm everywhere and breed anew; in Henan and Hebei families have no reserves—one failed harvest means exile, and the realm's security hangs in the balance.

sentences.zh: 且討蝗縱不能盡，不愈於養以遺患乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, even if pursuing locusts cannot eliminate them all, is that not better than nurturing them to leave a calamity behind?
translations.idiomatic: Even if extermination cannot be complete, is that not still better than tolerating them and bequeathing disaster?

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 黃門監盧懷慎曰：「凡天災，安可以人力制也！

translations.literal: Huangmen Supervisor Lu Huaishen said: "Every heavenly calamity—how can it be controlled by human strength!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaishen, Supervisor of the Yellow Gate, objected: "Heaven sends calamities—how can mere human effort restrain them!

sentences.zh: 且殺蟲多，必戾和氣。

translations.literal: Moreover, killing many insects will surely offend the harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, mass slaughter of living things must disturb the cosmic harmony.

sentences.zh: 願公思之。」

translations.literal: I hope you will reflect on this."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「昔楚王吞蛭而厥疾瘳，叔敖斷虵福乃降。

translations.literal: Chong said: "Formerly King Zhuang of Chu swallowed a leech and his illness was cured; Sunshu Ao cut a snake and blessings then descended.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "King Zhuang of Chu once swallowed a leech and was healed; Sunshu Ao killed a serpent and fortune followed.

sentences.zh: 今蝗幸可驅，若縱之，穀且盡，如百姓何？

translations.literal: Now the locusts fortunately can be driven off; if you let them go, grain will soon be exhausted—what of the common people?
translations.idiomatic: These locusts can still be driven away; if we release them, the harvest will be lost—what then becomes of the people?

sentences.zh: 殺蟲救人，禍歸於崇，不以諉公也！」

translations.literal: To kill insects and save men—the calamity falls on Chong; I will not shift it onto you, sir!
translations.idiomatic: If slaying pests saves lives, let the blame fall on me—not on you, my lord!

sentences.zh: 蝗害訖息。

translations.literal: The locust calamity finally ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The locust plague was finally brought under control.

sentences.zh: 於是，帝方躬萬機，朝夕詢逮，它宰相畏帝威決，皆謙憚，唯獨崇佐裁決，故得專任。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor was personally attending to myriad affairs, inquiring morning and evening; the other chancellors feared the Emperor's stern resolve and were all deferential—only Chong alone assisted in deciding, and so he gained sole responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now personally directed state affairs and consulted Chong morning and evening. Other chancellors, awed by his decisive authority, held back; only Chong assisted in judgment, and so held effective monopoly of power.

sentences.zh: 崇第賒僻，因近舍客廬。

translations.literal: Chong's residence was shabby and remote; he therefore lodged nearby in a guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's own house was dilapidated and out of the way, so he rented lodgings nearby.

sentences.zh: 會懷慎卒，崇病{痁}移告，凡大政事，帝必令源乾曜就咨焉。

translations.literal: When Huaishen died, Chong fell ill with ague and submitted leave; for every great government matter the Emperor would have Yuan Qianyao go consult him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaishen died, Chong fell ill with malaria and took leave; on every major policy question the emperor sent Yuan Qianyao to consult him.

sentences.zh: 乾曜所奏善，帝則曰：「是必崇畫之。」

translations.literal: When Qianyao's memorials were good, the Emperor would say: "This must be Chong's drafting."
translations.idiomatic: When Qianyao's recommendations were sound, the emperor would say, "Chong must have drafted this."

sentences.zh: 有不合，則曰：「胡不問崇？」

translations.literal: When they were not fitting, he would say: "Why not ask Chong?"
translations.idiomatic: When they missed the mark, he would say, "Why did you not consult Chong?"

sentences.zh: 乾曜謝其未也，乃已。

translations.literal: Qianyao would apologize for not having done so, and only then would it end.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao would apologize for the oversight, and the matter would rest.

sentences.zh: 帝欲崇自近，詔徙寓四方館，日遣問食飲起居，高醫、尚食踵道。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished Chong nearby; he ordered him moved to lodge at the Four Directions Hostel, daily sending inquiries after food, drink, and daily life; eminent physicians and the Palace Provisioners followed in his track.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing Chong close at hand, the emperor had him moved to the Four Directions Hostel and sent daily inquiries about his meals and health; court physicians and palace caterers attended him in succession.

sentences.zh: 崇以館局華大，不敢居。

translations.literal: Chong, because the hostel establishment was grand, dared not dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Chong found the hostel too grand and declined to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 帝使語崇曰：「恨不處禁中，此何避？」

translations.literal: The Emperor had someone tell Chong: "I regret you are not housed within the Forbidden precincts—what is there to avoid here?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word: "I only regret you are not inside the palace itself—why shrink from this?"

sentences.zh: 久之，紫微史趙誨受夷人賕，當死。

translations.literal: After a long while, Assistant in the Bureau of Astronomy Zhao Hui received bribes from barbarians and should die.
translations.idiomatic: In time Zhao Hui, an assistant in the Bureau of Astronomy, was found to have taken bribes from foreigners and faced execution.

sentences.zh: 崇素親倚，署奏營減，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Chong had long been intimate with and relied on him; he drafted a memorial seeking reduction of sentence—the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, who had long favored him, submitted a plea for leniency; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 時曲赦京師，惟誨不原。

translations.literal: At the time there was a general amnesty in the capital, but only Hui was not forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed for the capital, but Zhao Hui alone was excluded.

sentences.zh: 崇惶懼，上還宰政，引宋璟代，乃以開府儀同三司罷政事。

translations.literal: Chong was fearful; he returned the chancellorship, brought in Song Jing to replace him, and was dismissed from government affairs with the title of Defender-in-Chief and Concurrent Supervisor of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for himself, Chong resigned the chancellorship, recommended Song Jing as successor, and was relieved of office with the honorific rank of Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 帝將幸東都，而太廟屋自壞，帝問宰相，宋璟、蘇頲同對曰：「三年之喪未終，不可以行幸。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital when the Ancestral Temple hall collapsed of itself; the Emperor asked the chancellors; Song Jing and Su Ting together replied: "The three-year mourning is not yet ended—you may not go on a progress.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a journey to the Eastern Capital, the ancestral temple roof collapsed. He asked his chancellors; Song Jing and Su Ting jointly replied, "The three-year mourning period is not complete—you must not travel.

sentences.zh: 壞壓之變，天所以示教戒，陛下宜停東巡，修德以答至譴。」

translations.literal: The change of collapse and crushing—Heaven thereby shows teaching and warning; Your Majesty ought to stop the eastern tour and cultivate virtue to answer this utmost reprimand."
translations.idiomatic: This collapse is Heaven's warning. Your Majesty should cancel the eastern tour and cultivate virtue to answer the divine rebuke."

sentences.zh: 帝以問崇，對曰：「臣聞隋取苻堅故殿以營廟，而唐因之。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned Chong, who replied: "I have heard that Sui took Fu Jian's old hall to build the temple, and Tang followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Chong, who answered, "I have heard that the Sui dynasty took Fu Jian's old hall to build the temple, and Tang inherited it.

sentences.zh: 且山有朽壞乃崩，況木積年而木自當蠹乎。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a mountain has rotten decay it then collapses—how much more when wood has accumulated for years should the wood itself become worm-eaten?
translations.idiomatic: Mountains collapse when their timbers rot—how much more should beams that have stood for years be eaten by worms?

sentences.zh: 但壞與行會，不緣行而壞。

translations.literal: Only the collapse and the journey coincided; it did not collapse because of the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The collapse merely coincided with your planned journey; the journey did not cause the collapse.

sentences.zh: 且陛下以關中無年，輪餉告勞，因以幸東都，所以為人不為己也。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty, because Guanzhong had no harvest and transport of provisions reported exhaustion, thereupon visited the Eastern Capital—this was for others and not for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you travel east because Guanzhong has no harvest and grain transport is exhausted—this is for the people, not for yourself.

sentences.zh: 百司已戒，供擬既具，請車駕如行期。

translations.literal: The hundred offices are already warned; supplies and preparations are complete—I beg the imperial carriage to keep to the scheduled date of travel.
translations.idiomatic: All ministries are prepared and supplies ready. I beg Your Majesty to depart on schedule.

sentences.zh: 舊廟難復完，盡奉神主舍太極殿？

translations.literal: The old temple cannot easily be made whole again—should we move all spirit tablets to lodge in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate?
translations.idiomatic: The old temple cannot be fully restored—might we house the spirit tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate?

sentences.zh: 更作新廟，申誠奉，大孝之德也。」

translations.literal: To build a new temple anew and declare sincere service—that is the virtue of great filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: To build a new temple and offer sincere worship—that is the height of filial devotion."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言正契朕意。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your words exactly match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your counsel matches my own mind exactly."

sentences.zh: 賜絹二百匹，詔所司如崇言，天子遂東。

translations.literal: He bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and ordered the offices to act as Chong said; the Son of Heaven thereupon went east.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Chong with two hundred bolts of silk, ordered the ministries to follow his plan, and proceeded east.

sentences.zh: 因詔五日一參，入閣供奉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered attendance every five days, entering the Pavilion to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was thereafter summoned to court every five days to attend in the inner pavilion.

sentences.zh: 八年，授太子少保，以疾不拜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent but did not accept on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was named Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈揚州大都督，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief of Yangzhou; his posthumous title was Wenxian (Literary and Illustrious).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Defender-in-Chief of Yangzhou with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 十七年，追贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was further posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was further posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇析貲產，令諸子各有定分。

translations.literal: Chong divided his property and ordered each of his sons to have a fixed allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Chong divided his estate and assigned each son a fixed share.

sentences.zh: 治令曰：

translations.literal: His testament order said:
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions read:

sentences.zh: 比見達宦之裔多貧困，至銖尺是競，無論曲直，均受絜，詆。

translations.literal: I have lately observed that descendants of eminent officials are mostly poor; they compete even over specks and measures; regardless of right or wrong, all alike suffer calumny and vilification.
translations.idiomatic: I have often seen children of great ministers end in poverty, quarreling over trifles; whether in the right or wrong, all alike are mocked and slandered.

sentences.zh: 田宅水磑既共有之，至相推倚以頓廢。

translations.literal: Fields, houses, and water-mills—once jointly held—come to leaning on one another to mutual ruin and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: When fields, houses, and mills are held in common, heirs shove responsibility onto one another until the property is ruined.

sentences.zh: 陸賈、石苞，古達者也，亦先有定分，以絕後爭。

translations.literal: Lu Jia and Shi Bao were men of penetrating wisdom in antiquity; they too first had fixed allotments to cut off later strife.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia and Shi Bao, wise men of old, likewise fixed shares in advance to forestall later disputes.

sentences.zh: 昔楊震、趙明、盧植、張奐咸以薄葬，知真識去身，貴速朽耳。

translations.literal: Formerly Yang Zhen, Zhao Ming, Lu Zhi, and Zhang Huan all used simple burial—they knew truth and understood departure from the body, valuing swift decay.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhen, Zhao Ming, Lu Zhi, and Zhang Huan all chose plain burials, knowing the body is fleeting and honoring swift return to dust.

sentences.zh: 夫厚葬之家流於俗，以奢靡為孝，令死者戮屍暴骸，可不痛哉！

translations.literal: Those families of lavish burial follow custom, taking extravagance as filial piety, causing the dead to suffer dismembered corpses and exposed bones—can this not grieve one!
translations.idiomatic: Families that bury lavishly follow fashion, mistaking extravagance for filial piety—yet the dead are dug up and desecrated. How pitiful!

sentences.zh: 死者無知，自同糞土，豈煩奢葬；

translations.literal: The dead have no awareness; they are themselves like dung and earth—why trouble over lavish burial;
translations.idiomatic: The dead know nothing; they are no different from soil—why waste wealth on grand tombs;

sentences.zh: 使其有知，神不在柩，何用破貲徇侈乎？

translations.literal: if they had awareness, the spirit would not be in the coffin—what use to squander assets and pursue extravagance?
translations.idiomatic: and if they did know, their spirits would not linger in the coffin—why squander fortune on vanity?

sentences.zh: 吾亡，斂以常服，四時衣各一稱。

translations.literal: When I die, let me be enshrouded in ordinary dress, one set of season's clothing for each of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, dress me in ordinary clothes—one suit for each season, no more.

sentences.zh: 性不喜冠衣，毋以入墓。

translations.literal: By nature I do not love caps and robes—do not place them in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: I never cared for formal caps and gowns in life—do not bury them with me.

sentences.zh: 紫衣玉帶，足便於體。

translations.literal: Purple robe and jade belt are quite convenient for the body.
translations.idiomatic: Purple robes and jade belts are comfortable enough for daily wear.

sentences.zh: 今之佛經，羅什所譯，姚興與之對翻，而興命不延，國亦隨滅。

translations.literal: Today's Buddhist sutras were translated by Kumarajiva; Yao Xing paired with him in face-to-face translation—and yet Xing's life was not prolonged and the state also followed into extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist scriptures we have were translated by Kumarajiva while Yao Xing sat opposite him—yet Yao Xing died young and his kingdom perished.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝身為寺奴，齊胡太后以六宮入道，皆亡國殄家。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang served as a temple slave; Empress Dowager Hu of Northern Qi had the six palaces enter the Way—all perished state and exterminated family.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang became a temple servant; the Northern Qi Empress Dowager Hu sent the palace women to take vows—both dynasties were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 近孝和皇帝發使贖生，太平公主、武三思等度人造寺，身嬰夷戮，為天下笑。

translations.literal: Recently Emperor Xiahe sent envoys to ransom living creatures; Princess Taiping, Wu Sansi, and others tonsured people and built temples—they personally met barbarous execution and became the world's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: More recently Emperor Xiahe sent agents to buy the release of animals; Princess Taiping, Wu Sansi, and others ordained followers and built temples—yet they were executed and became a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 五帝之時，父不喪子，兄不哭弟，致仁壽，無凶短也。

translations.literal: In the time of the Five Emperors, fathers did not mourn sons, elder brothers did not weep for younger brothers—they attained benevolence and longevity, without short and calamitous lives.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Five Emperors, fathers did not bury sons nor brothers mourn brothers—yet they lived long in peace without untimely death.

sentences.zh: 下逮三王，國祚延久，其臣則彭祖、老聃皆得長齡，此時無佛，豈抄經鑄像力邪？

translations.literal: Down to the Three Kings, national fortune lasted long; their ministers Peng Zu and Laozi all attained long years—at that time there was no Buddha; was it the power of copying sutras and casting images?
translations.idiomatic: Through the Three Dynasties, states endured for centuries; Peng Zu and Laozi lived to great age—before Buddhism existed. Did they owe their longevity to copying sutras and casting images?

sentences.zh: 緣死喪造經像，以為追福。

translations.literal: Owing to death and mourning they make sutras and images, thinking to pursue blessing.
translations.idiomatic: People now commission scriptures and statues at funerals, imagining they can buy merit for the dead.

sentences.zh: 夫死者生之常，古所不免，彼經與像何所施為？

translations.literal: Death is the constant of life; antiquity could not avoid it—what use are those sutras and images?
translations.idiomatic: Death is the natural end of life, unavoidable since antiquity—of what use are sutras and statues?

sentences.zh: 兒曹慎不得為此！

translations.literal: You boys must take care never to do this!
translations.idiomatic: My sons: see that you never do such things!

sentences.zh: 崇尤長吏道，處決無淹思。

translations.literal: Chong was especially skilled in the way of officials; in deciding cases he had no lingering thought.
translations.idiomatic: Chong excelled above all in the arts of governance; he decided matters without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 三為宰相，常兼兵部，故屯戊斥候、士馬儲械，無不諳記。

translations.literal: Thrice he was chancellor, often concurrently holding the Ministry of War; therefore stationing garrisons, scouts, soldiers, horses, stored arms and equipment—none was he not versed in by heart.
translations.idiomatic: Three times chancellor, he usually also headed the Ministry of War, and knew by heart every garrison, scout post, troop disposition, and store of arms.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初立，賓禮大臣故老，雅尊遇崇，每見便殿，必為之興，去輒臨軒以送，它相莫如也。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first took the throne he treated old ministers with guest rites and greatly honored Chong; every time he saw him in the side hall he would rise for him, and when he left would step to the front of the hall to see him off—no other chancellor was like this.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first ascended the throne he honored veteran ministers; Chong he treated with special esteem—rising whenever Chong entered the side hall and walking to the front steps to see him off, a courtesy granted no other chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時承權戚幹政之後，綱紀大壞，先天末，宰相至十七人，台省要職不可數。

translations.literal: At the time, inheriting after powerful kin interfered in government, law and discipline were greatly broken; at the end of the Xiantian era chancellors reached seventeen, and important posts of the Censorate and Secretariat could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited a court where powerful consort clans had shattered discipline; by the end of the Xiantian era there were seventeen chancellors and innumerable key posts in the secretariats and censorate.

sentences.zh: 崇常先有司罷冗職，修制度，擇百官各當其材，請無廣釋道，無數移吏。

translations.literal: Chong often had the offices first abolish redundant posts, repair institutions, choose the hundred offices each to fit his talent, and request no expansion of Buddhist teachings and no frequent transfer of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Chong pressed agencies to eliminate redundant offices, restore proper regulations, assign men to posts matching their abilities, curb Buddhist patronage, and stop constant reshuffling of officials.

sentences.zh: 繇是天子責成于下，而權歸於上矣。

translations.literal: Hence the Son of Heaven placed responsibility on those below, and power returned to those above.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the emperor held subordinates accountable while authority returned to the throne.

sentences.zh: 然資權譎。

translations.literal: Yet he was by nature crafty in power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was also resourceful and calculating in the use of power.

sentences.zh: 始為同州，張說以素憾，諷趙彥昭劾崇。

translations.literal: When he was first prefect of Tongzhou, Zhang Shuo because of old resentment goaded Zhao Yanzhao to impeach Chong.
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of Tongzhou, he incurred Zhang Shuo's lasting enmity; Shuo induced Zhao Yanzhao to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 及當國，說懼，潛詣岐王申款。

translations.literal: When he held the state, Shuo feared him; he secretly went to Prince of Qi to declare his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chong held power, Shuo grew afraid and secretly sought favor with the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 崇它日朝，眾趨出，崇曳踵為有疾狀，帝召問之，對曰：「臣損足。」

translations.literal: Another day at court, when the crowd hurried out, Chong dragged his heels in a manner of illness; the Emperor summoned and questioned him; he replied: "Your servant has injured his foot."
translations.idiomatic: On another court day, as officials hurried out, Chong limped as if lame. The emperor called him back and asked; Chong said, "I have hurt my foot."

sentences.zh: 曰：「無甚痛乎？」

translations.literal: He said: "Not much pain then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Does it hurt much?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣心有憂，痛不在足。」

translations.literal: He said: "Your servant's heart has worry; the pain is not in the foot."
translations.idiomatic: Chong answered, "My heart is troubled—the pain is not in my foot."

sentences.zh: 問以故，曰：「岐王陛下愛弟，張說輔臣，而密乘車出入王家，恐為所誤，故憂之。」

translations.literal: Asked the reason, he said: "The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's beloved younger brother; Zhang Shuo is a assisting minister—yet he secretly rides in a carriage in and out of the princely house; I fear he will be led astray, and so I worry."
translations.idiomatic: Pressed for the cause, he said, "The Prince of Qi is your beloved brother and Zhang Shuo a chief minister—yet Shuo visits the prince's house by night in a closed carriage. I fear he may lead the prince astray, and that is my worry."

sentences.zh: 於是出說相州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shuo was sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuo was thereupon exiled as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏知古，崇所引，及同列，稍輕之，出攝吏部尚書，知東都選，知古憾焉。

translations.literal: Wei Zhigu was one Chong had introduced; when they were colleagues Chong gradually slighted him; he was sent out to act as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and to oversee selection at the Eastern Capital—Zhigu resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu, whom Chong had promoted, was gradually slighted once they shared rank; Chong had him sent to oversee personnel selection at Luoyang, and Zhigu resented the demotion.

sentences.zh: 時崇二子在洛，通賓客饋遺，憑舊請托。

translations.literal: At the time Chong's two sons were in Luoyang, receiving guests' gifts and relying on old ties for requests.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chong's two sons in Luoyang entertained guests, accepted gifts, and traded on their father's influence.

sentences.zh: 知古歸，悉以聞。

translations.literal: When Zhigu returned, he reported all to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, Zhigu reported everything to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝召崇曰：「卿子才乎，皆安在？」

translations.literal: Another day the Emperor summoned Chong and said: "Are your sons talented? Where are they all?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor asked Chong, "Are your sons capable? Where are they now?"

sentences.zh: 崇揣知帝意，曰：「臣二子分司東都，其為人多欲而寡慎，是必嘗以事幹魏知古。」

translations.literal: Chong guessed the Emperor's intent and said: "Your servant's two sons serve in office at the Eastern Capital; in conduct they are much desirous and little cautious—they must certainly have once had business with Wei Zhigu."
translations.idiomatic: Chong divined the emperor's meaning and replied, "My two sons hold posts in Luoyang. They are greedy and careless—they must have importuned Wei Zhigu."

sentences.zh: 帝始以崇私其子，或為隱，微以言動之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had first thought Chong favored his sons and might conceal it, and subtly moved him with words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had suspected Chong would shield his sons and probed him obliquely."

sentences.zh: 及聞，乃大喜，問：「安從得之？」

translations.literal: When he heard this he was greatly pleased and asked: "How did you learn of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this frank answer, he was delighted and asked, "How did you know?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「知古，臣所薦也，臣子必謂其見德而請之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Zhigu was one your servant recommended; my sons would surely think he saw their virtue and approached him with requests."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "Zhigu is a man I advanced; my sons would assume he owed them favor and approached him."

sentences.zh: 帝於是愛崇不私而薄知古，欲斥之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon loved Chong for not being partial and thought lightly of Zhigu, wishing to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired Chong's impartiality and turned against Zhigu, intending to remove him.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「臣子無狀，橈陛下法，而逐知古，外必謂陛下私臣。」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Your servant's sons are unseemly, bending Your Majesty's law—yet if Zhigu is driven off, outside they will surely say Your Majesty favors your servant."
translations.idiomatic: Chong pleaded, "My sons have misbehaved, yet if you dismiss Zhigu, outsiders will say you favor me."

sentences.zh: 乃止，然卒罷為工部尚書。

translations.literal: He stopped there, but in the end Zhigu was dismissed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented, but Zhigu was eventually demoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇始名元崇，以與突厥叱剌同名，武后時以字行；

translations.literal: Chong was originally named Yuanchong; because it was the same name as the Türk Chila, in Empress Wu's time he went by his courtesy name;
translations.idiomatic: Chong was originally named Yuanchong; because this matched the name of a Türk chieftain, he used his courtesy name during Empress Wu's reign;

sentences.zh: 至開元世，避帝號，更以今名。

translations.literal: in the Kaiyuan era, avoiding the imperial taboo, he changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: and in the Kaiyuan era, to avoid the emperor's taboo, adopted his present name.

sentences.zh: 三子：彝、異、弈，皆至卿、刺史。

translations.literal: Three sons: Yi, Yi, and Yi—all reached minister and prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Yi, Yi, and Yi—each rising to ministerial rank or provincial governorship.

sentences.zh: 子 弈弈少修謹。

translations.literal: Son Yi—Yi from youth was careful and proper in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was from youth careful and self-restrained.

sentences.zh: 始，崇欲使不越官次而習知吏道，故自右千牛進至太子舍人，皆平遷。

translations.literal: At first Chong wished him not to overleap ranks in office yet to learn and know the clerks' way; therefore from Right Thousand Bull onward to Crown Prince Attendant—all were level promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had wished him to learn administration without skipping ranks; from Right Palace Guard through Crown Prince's Attendant, every promotion was by regular step.

sentences.zh: 開元中，有事五陵，有司以鷹犬從，弈曰：「非禮也。」

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, when attending to affairs at the Five Mausoleums, the offices had hawk-dogs follow; Yi said: "This is not ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, when rites were performed at the imperial mausoleums, officials brought hawks and hounds; Yi objected, "This is improper."

sentences.zh: 奏罷之。

translations.literal: He memorialized and had it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized and the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 請治劇，為睢陽太守，召授太僕卿。

translations.literal: He requested to govern Ju, served as prefect of Suiyang, and was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Herds.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked to administer Ju, became prefect of Suiyang, then was recalled and made Grand Master of the Herds.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Later he was Vice Minister of the Right in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Minister of the Right.

sentences.zh: 子閎，居右相牛仙客幕府。

translations.literal: His son Hong served on the staff of the Right Chancellor Niu Xianke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong was in the secretariat of Right Chancellor Niu Xianke.

sentences.zh: 仙客病甚，閎強使薦弈及盧奐為宰相，仙客妻以聞，閎坐死，弈貶永陽太守，卒。

translations.literal: When Xianke was gravely ill, Hong forcibly had him recommend Yi and Lu Huan as chancellors; Xianke's wife reported it. Hong was executed for the crime; Yi was demoted to prefect of Yongyang and died there.
translations.idiomatic: As Xianke lay dying, Hong forced him to nominate Yi and Lu Huan for the chancellorship. The wife informed the throne; Hong was put to death, Yi was banished to Yongyang as prefect, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 合曾孫合、勖。

translations.literal: Great-grandsons: He and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandsons were He and Xu.

sentences.zh: 合，元和中進士及第，調武功尉，善詩，世號姚武功者。

translations.literal: He, in the Yuanhe era passed the jinshi examination, was appointed sheriff of Wugong, excelled at poetry, and the age called him "Yao of Wugong."
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the Yuanhe reign, served as sheriff of Wugong, and became famed as a poet—the world knew him as Yao of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，累轉給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance censor and in succession rose to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to surveillance censor and eventually to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 奉先、馮翊二縣民訴牛羊使奪其田，詔美原主簿硃儔覆按，猥以田歸使，合劾發其私，以地還民。

translations.literal: The people of Fengxian and Fengyi counties sued the cattle-and-sheep commissioner for seizing their fields; an edict ordered Meiyuan registrar Zhu Chou to reinvestigate. Basely he returned the land to the commissioner. He impeached him, exposing his private dealings, and returned the land to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When peasants in Fengxian and Fengyi accused the cattle-and-sheep commissioner of seizing their fields, the court sent Zhu Chou of Meiyuan to review the case; he corruptly awarded the land to the commissioner. He exposed the fraud and restored the fields to their owners.

sentences.zh: 曆陝虢觀察使，終秘書監。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner of the Shaanxi-Guo observation circuit and ended his career as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shaanxi-Guo observation commissioner and died as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 勗勖字斯勤。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Xu—courtesy name Sijin.
translations.idiomatic: Another great-grandson, Xu, whose courtesy name was Sijin.

sentences.zh: 長慶初擢進士第，數為使府表辟，進監察御史，佐鹽鐵使務。

translations.literal: In the early Changqing era he passed the jinshi degree; several times he was summoned by regional staffs; he advanced to surveillance censor and assisted in the salt-and-iron commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Changqing he took the jinshi; repeatedly recruited to provincial staffs, he became a surveillance censor and helped run salt-and-iron affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷諫議大夫，更湖、常二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Remonstrance Grandee and then exchanged posts as prefect of Hu and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Remonstrance Grandee and served in turn as prefect of Hu and Chang.

sentences.zh: 為宰相李德裕厚善。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with the chancellor Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was a warm friend of Chancellor Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 及德裕為令狐綯等譖逐，擿索支黨，無敢通勞問；

translations.literal: When Deyu was slandered and driven out by Linghu Tao and others, they rooted out his partisans, and none dared to visit him in sympathy;
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu was framed by Linghu Tao and exiled, investigators hunted his allies, and no one dared even send condolences;

sentences.zh: 既海上，家無資，病無湯劑，勖數饋餉候問，不傅時為厚薄。

translations.literal: once he was at sea, his household had no means, and when ill he had no medicines—Xu repeatedly sent provisions and inquired after him, not trimming his kindness to the temper of the times.
translations.idiomatic: banished overseas, Deyu was penniless and without medicine; Xu kept sending food and asking after him, heedless of whether the court favored or hated him.

sentences.zh: 終夔王傅。

translations.literal: He ended as tutor to the Prince of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as tutor to the Prince of Kui.

sentences.zh: 自作壽藏于萬安山南原崇塋之旁，署兆曰「寂居穴」，墳曰「復真堂」，中剟土為床曰「化台」，而刻石告後世。

translations.literal: He himself made a longevity vault on the south plain of Mount Wan'an beside the lofty ancestral tomb, marked the site "Cave of Silent Dwelling," the mound "Hall of Returning to Truth," hollowed earth within for a couch called "Platform of Transformation," and carved stone to inform posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared his own tomb on the southern slope of Mount Wan'an next to the family grave, naming the plot the Cave of Silent Dwelling and the chamber the Hall of Returning to Truth; inside he cut an earthen bed called the Platform of Transformation and left an inscription for later ages.

sentences.zh: 宋璟，邢州南和人。

translations.literal: Song Jing—Jing was a native of Nanhe in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing was from Nanhe in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七世祖弁為元魏吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Bian was Minister of Personnel under Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations back, Bian had been Northern Wei Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 璟耿介有大節，好學，工文辭，舉進士中第。

translations.literal: Jing was upright and possessed great integrity, loved learning, was skilled in literary composition, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and high-principled, he studied hard, wrote well, and earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 調上党尉，為監察御史，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed sheriff of Shangdang, became a surveillance censor, and was promoted to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He served as sheriff of Shangdang, then surveillance censor, then Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 居官鯁正，武后高其才。

translations.literal: In office he was unbending and correct; Empress Wu valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was famously incorruptible; Empress Wu admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 張易之誣御史大夫魏元忠有不臣語，引張說為驗，將廷辯，說惶遽，璟謂說曰：「名義至重，不可陷正人以求苟免。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi falsely accused Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong of disloyal speech, citing Zhang Yue as witness; when they were to debate at court, Yue was in panic. Jing said to Yue: "Reputation and duty weigh most heavily—you must not frame an upright man to seek a careless escape.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi charged Wei Yuanzhong with treasonous words and named Zhang Yue as witness. As the court hearing neared, Yue panicked. Jing told him, "Honor matters more than your skin—do not ruin an innocent man to save yourself.

sentences.zh: 緣此受謫，芬香多矣。

translations.literal: If you suffer demotion for this, your fragrance will be the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Even exile for telling the truth would leave you fragrant in history.

sentences.zh: 若不測者，吾且叩閣救，將與子偕死。」

translations.literal: If worse should come, I shall beat on the palace gate to rescue you and die with you."
translations.idiomatic: If they threaten your life, I will petition at the gate and face death at your side."

sentences.zh: 說感其言，以實對，元忠免死。

translations.literal: Yue was moved by his words, answered according to the facts, and Yuanzhong escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Yue testified honestly, and Yuanzhong was spared.

sentences.zh: 璟後遷左台御史中丞，會飛書告張昌宗引相工觀吉凶者，璟請窮治，後曰：「易之等已自言於朕。」

translations.literal: Later Jing was promoted to Left Bureau Censor-in-Chief. When an anonymous letter reported that Zhang Changzong had brought in a physiognomist to read fortunes, Jing requested a thorough investigation. The Empress said: "Yizhi and the others have already confessed to Us."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Bureau Censor-in-Chief, he learned that Zhang Changzong had consulted a fortune-teller; he demanded a full inquiry. The Empress replied, "Yizhi has already told me himself."

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「謀反無容以首原，請下吏明國法。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Treason admits no pardon for coming forward first—please hand them to the officials and make clear the law of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered, "Rebellion cannot be forgiven for a confession—put them under the law.

sentences.zh: 易之等貴寵，臣言之且有禍，然激於義，雖死不悔。」

translations.literal: Yizhi and the others are exalted favorites; if I speak I shall yet have disaster—yet stirred by righteousness, though I die I shall not repent."
translations.idiomatic: They are the emperor's favorites; I may be ruined for accusing them, but duty leaves me no retreat, even at the cost of my life."

sentences.zh: 後不懌，姚崇遽傳詔令出，璟曰：「今親奉德音，不煩宰相擅宣王命。」

translations.literal: The Empress was displeased; Yao Chong hastily transmitted an edict ordering him out. Jing said: "Today I personally receive the sovereign's gracious command—there is no need for the chancellor on his own authority to proclaim the royal word."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress frowned; Yao Chong rushed out an edict to dismiss him. Jing objected, "I am hearing the Son of Heaven himself—why should a minister announce his will unbidden?"

sentences.zh: 後意解，許收易之等就獄。

translations.literal: The Empress's anger eased, and she permitted Yizhi and the others to be taken into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Her mood softened, and she allowed Yizhi and his brother to be jailed.

sentences.zh: 俄詔原之，敕二張詣璟謝，璟不見，曰：「公事公言之，若私見，法無私也。」

translations.literal: Soon an edict pardoned them and ordered the two Zhangs to go to Jing to apologize; Jing would not see them, saying: "Public affairs are spoken in public; if you wish a private meeting, the law knows no private favor."
translations.idiomatic: They were quickly forgiven and sent to apologize; Jing refused the audience: "State business belongs in court; private visits have no place in the law."

sentences.zh: 顧左右歎曰：「吾悔不先碎豎子首而令亂國經。」

translations.literal: Turning to those beside him he sighed: "I regret I did not first smash those wretches' heads and let them throw the state's norms into chaos."
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "I should have broken their necks before they could warp the empire's order.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴朝堂，二張列卿三品，璟階六品，居下坐。

translations.literal: Once at a feast in the imperial hall, the two Zhangs ranked as ministers of the third grade while Jing, of the sixth grade in rank, sat below.
translations.idiomatic: At a palace banquet the Zhang brothers sat among third-rank ministers while Jing, only sixth rank, took the lower seat.

sentences.zh: 易之諂事璟，虛位揖曰：「公第一人，何下坐？」

translations.literal: Yizhi fawned on Jing, left an empty seat and bowed, saying: "You, sir, are the foremost man—why sit below?"
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi flattered him, yielding a seat: "You are first among us—why take the lower place?"

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「才劣品卑，卿謂第一何邪？」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Talent is poor and rank is low—why do you call me foremost?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing replied, "My talent is mean and my rank humble—what makes me first?

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷以易之等內寵，不名其官，呼易之「五郎」，昌宗「六郎」。

translations.literal: At that time the court, because Yizhi and the others enjoyed inner favor, did not name their offices and called Yizhi "Fifth Lord" and Changzong "Sixth Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhangs were the empress's favorites, officials avoided their titles and called them Fifth Lord and Sixth Lord.

sentences.zh: 鄭善果謂璟曰：「公奈何謂五郎為卿？」

translations.literal: Zheng Shanguo said to Jing: "How can you, sir, call the Fifth Lord 'lord'?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanguo protested, "Why do you address the Fifth Lord as 'lord'?"

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「以官正當為卿。

translations.literal: Jing said: "By their office it is proper to call them 'lord.
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered, "By rank they are lords—that is the proper form.

sentences.zh: 君非其家奴，何郎之雲？」

translations.literal: You are not their household slave—why speak of 'lord' in that way?"
translations.idiomatic: You are not their servant—why ape their flattery with talk of 'lords'?

sentences.zh: 會有喪，告滿入朝，公卿以次謁，通禮意。

translations.literal: When he had mourning obligations and, after leave expired, entered court, the ministers and grandees called in turn to pay respects and exchange ritual courtesies.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning leave he returned to court; colleagues visited in order to exchange condolences and civilities.

sentences.zh: 易之等後至，促步前，璟舉笏卻揖唯唯。

translations.literal: Yizhi and the others arrived later, hurried forward with quick steps; Jing raised his tablet and stepped back, bowing in assent with many "yeses."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangs came late, rushing ahead; Jing lifted his ivory tablet, stepped aside, and bowed with perfunctory deference.

sentences.zh: 故積怨，常欲中傷，後知之，得免。

translations.literal: Hence they nursed resentment and often wished to strike at him from within; the Empress learned of it, and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: They hated him for it and plotted his ruin; only the Empress's notice spared him.

sentences.zh: 然以數忤旨，詔按獄揚州，璟奏：「按州縣，才監察御史職耳。」

translations.literal: Yet because he repeatedly offended the throne's intent, an edict ordered him to investigate cases at Yangzhou. Jing memorialized: "Investigating prefectures and counties is only the duty of a surveillance censor."
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly defying her wishes, he was ordered to Yangzhou to hear cases. He protested, "County investigations are work for a surveillance censor alone."

sentences.zh: 又詔按幽州都督屈突仲翔，辭曰：「御史中丞非大事不出使。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered him to investigate Qu Tu Zhongxiang, military commissioner of Youzhou; he declined: "The censor-in-chief does not go on mission unless the affair is grave.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent him to probe Youzhou commissioner Qu Tu Zhongxiang; he refused: "A censor-in-chief leaves the capital only for great matters.

sentences.zh: 仲翔罪止贓，今使臣往，此必有危臣者。」

translations.literal: Zhongxiang's crime is only corruption—if you now send me, there must be someone who means to endanger me."
translations.idiomatic: His offense is mere bribery; dispatching me now means someone wants me dead on the road."

sentences.zh: 既而詔副李嶠使隴、蜀，璟復言：「隴右無變，臣以中丞副李嶠，非朝廷故事。」

translations.literal: Soon an edict made him deputy to Li Jiao on mission to Long and Shu; Jing again said: "There is no disturbance in Longyou; for me as censor-in-chief to assist Li Jiao is not court precedent."
translations.idiomatic: He was then named Li Jiao's deputy to Long and Shu; again he objected: "Longyou is quiet—there is no precedent for a censor-in-chief to serve under Li Jiao."

sentences.zh: 終辭。

translations.literal: In the end he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to go.

sentences.zh: 易之初冀璟出則劾奏誅之，計不行，乃伺璟〗家婚禮，將遣客刺殺之。

translations.literal: Yizhi at first hoped that once Jing left court he could memorialize and have him executed; the plan failed. He then watched Jing's household wedding ceremony and was about to send agents to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi had hoped to destroy Jing once he left the capital; foiled, he planned to murder him at his son's wedding.

sentences.zh: 有告璟者，璟乘庳車舍他所，刺不得發。

translations.literal: Someone informed Jing; Jing rode a low carriage and lodged elsewhere, and the assassination could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Warned in time, Jing traveled in a humble cart and stayed elsewhere; the killers never struck.

sentences.zh: 俄二張死，乃免。

translations.literal: Soon the two Zhangs died, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhang brothers fell, the danger passed.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為吏部侍郎。
