translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years of Shenlong he became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 中宗嘉其直，令兼諫議大夫、內供奉，仗下與言得失。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong praised his forthrightness and ordered him also to serve as Remonstrance Grandee and inner attendant, speaking below the imperial halberd guard of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong admired his bluntness, made him Remonstrance Grandee and inner attendant, and allowed him to debate policy beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 武三思怙烝寵，數有請於璟。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi relied on his favor as the Empress's paramour and repeatedly made requests of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, bloated with the empress dowager's favor, often importuned Jing.

sentences.zh: 璟厲答曰：「今復子明辟，王宜以侯就第，安得尚幹朝政，獨不見產、祿事乎？」

translations.literal: Jing sternly answered: "Now the heir apparent is enlightened and the realm is at peace—the prince ought to take his marquisate and retire to his estate; how can he still meddle in court affairs? Have you alone not seen the affair of Lü Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing rebuked him: "The crown prince rules openly—the prince of Tang should return to his fief; why meddle in government? Have you forgotten Lü Lu?"

sentences.zh: 後韋月將告三思亂宮掖，三思諷有司論大逆不道，帝詔殊死，璟請付獄按罪，帝怒，岸巾出側門，謂璟曰：「朕謂已誅矣，尚何請？」

translations.literal: Later Wei Yuejiang reported that Sansi was disturbing the inner palace; Sansi prompted the offices to judge it capital treason. The Emperor decreed immediate death. Jing requested that he be handed to the prisons to establish guilt. The Emperor was angry, threw off his headcloth, went out the side gate, and said to Jing: "We thought he was already executed—why still petition?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yuejiang accused Sansi of corrupting the palace women, Sansi had him charged with treason. Zhongzong ordered summary execution. Jing demanded trial first. The emperor, furious, strode out a side door bareheaded: "I meant him dead already—why argue?"

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「人言後私三思，陛下不問即斬之，臣恐有竊議者，請按而後刑。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "People say the Empress Dowager favors Sansi—if Your Majesty executes without inquiry, I fear there will be whispered criticism; please investigate and then punish."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "The court whispers that the empress protects Sansi; killing without trial will look like favoritism—investigate, then punish."

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged the more.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「請先誅臣，不然，終不奉詔。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Please execute me first; otherwise I will never obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Kill me first, or I will not obey."

sentences.zh: 帝乃流月將嶺南。

translations.literal: The Emperor then exiled Yuejiang to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong banished Yuejiang to Lingnan instead.

sentences.zh: 會還京師，詔璟權檢校並州長史，未行，又檢校貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, an edict made Jing acting provisional prefect of Bingzhou; before he departed, he was again made acting provisional prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Chang'an, he was named acting Bingzhou prefect, then acting Beizhou prefect before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 時河北水，歲大饑，三思使斂封租，璟拒不與，故為所擠。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei suffered floods and famine in a great year; Sansi sent men to collect sealed rents; Jing refused to hand them over, and for this was squeezed out by him.
translations.idiomatic: Floods and famine ravaged Hebei; Sansi tried to seize the sealed grain rents; Jing refused, and Sansi had him pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 曆杭、相二州，政清毅，吏下無敢犯者。

translations.literal: He served Hang and Xiang prefectures; his government was clear and stern, and subordinate officials did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Hang and Xiang he ruled with icy integrity; none under him dared misconduct.

sentences.zh: 遷洛州長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，以吏部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Jing was appointed Minister of Personnel and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Tong rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ruizong he became Minister of Personnel and chancellor with Tong rank.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，兼右庶子。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was crown prince, Jing also served as Right Vice Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He doubled as Right Vice Guardian when Xuanzong was heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 先是崔湜、鄭愔典選，為戚近幹奪，至迎用二歲闕，猶不能給，更置比冬選，流品淆並，璟與侍郎李乂、盧從願澄革之，銓總平允。

translations.literal: Earlier Cui Shi and Zheng Yin had managed selection; for kin and favorites they seized appointments, so that even using two years' worth of vacancies they still could not supply demand; they further set a midwinter selection, and grades and ranks were confused together. Jing, with Vice Ministers Li Yi and Lu Congyuan, clarified and reformed it; the roster was overall fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi and Zheng Yin had packed the roster with kin and clients, even adding a winter quota, until ranks were hopelessly tangled. With Li Yi and Lu Congyuan he cleaned the lists and made appointments equitable.

sentences.zh: 太平公主不利東宮，嘗駐輦光範門，伺執政以諷。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping was ill-disposed toward the Eastern Palace; once she halted her carriage at Guangfan Gate to watch the chief ministers and offer pointed hints.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping opposed the crown prince; she once waited at Guangfan Gate to stare down the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「太子有大功，宗朝社稷主也，安得異議？」

translations.literal: Jing said: "The crown prince has great merit and is master of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain—how can there be a different opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing declared, "The heir has earned the throne in waiting—how dare anyone dispute his place?"

sentences.zh: 乃與姚崇白奏出公主諸王于外，帝不能用。

translations.literal: He and Yao Chong then jointly memorialized to have the princess and the princes sent outside the capital; the Emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yao Chong urged the emperor to remove the princess and imperial brothers from court; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 貶楚州刺史，曆兗冀魏三州、河北按察使，進幽州都督，以國子祭酒留守東都，遷雍州長史。

translations.literal: He was demoted to prefect of Chuzhou, served in succession Yan, Ji, and Wei, was Hebei investigation commissioner, advanced to military commissioner of Youzhou, was National University Chancellor and regent at the Eastern Capital, and was promoted to prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to Chuzhou, he governed Yan, Ji, and Wei in turn, inspected Hebei, became Youzhou commissioner, chancellor of the National University while guarding Luoyang, then prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元初，以雍州為京兆府，復為尹。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong, Yongzhou was made the Capital Metropolis Prefecture, and he again became its intendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyuan, Yongzhou became Jingzhao Prefecture and he again served as intendant.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫，坐小累為睦州刺史，徙廣州都督。

translations.literal: He advanced to Censor-in-Chief; for a minor fault he was made prefect of Muzhou and was transferred to military commissioner of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Censor-in-Chief, he suffered a small demerit and was sent to Muzhou, then to Guangzhou as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廣人以竹茅茨屋，多火。

translations.literal: The people of Guang used bamboo and thatch for houses, and fires were many.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese built hovels of bamboo and straw, and fires were constant.

sentences.zh: 璟教之陶瓦築堵，列邸肆，越俗始知棟宇利而無患災。

translations.literal: Jing taught them to fire tile and build walls, and set out rows of shops; the Yue custom then first knew the benefit of beam-and-pillar houses and was without the worry of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He taught them brick walls and tiled roofs and laid out market streets; the region learned durable housing and fewer calamities.

sentences.zh: 召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷吏部兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he became Minister of Personnel and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝幸東都，次崤穀，馳道隘，稽擁車騎，帝命黜河南尹李朝隱、知頓使王怡等官。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited the Eastern Capital; at Xiaogu Pass the imperial road was narrow and carriage and horsemen were delayed and crowded. The Emperor ordered the dismissal of Henan intendant Li Chaoyin, transit commissioner Wang Yi, and other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Touring the eastern capital, the emperor found the road at Xiaogu choked; he ordered Henan intendant Li Chaoyin and transit commissioner Wang Yi dismissed.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「陛下富春秋，今始巡守，以道不治而罪二臣，繇此相飭，後有受其蔽者。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Your Majesty is in the prime of life and has now begun touring and guarding the realm—if for the road not being well ordered you punish these two ministers, from this mutual caution later there will be those who suffer their concealment."
translations.idiomatic: Jing warned, "You are young and just began touring—punishing two men for a rough road will teach officials to hide problems from you."

sentences.zh: 帝遽命舍之。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately ordered them spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once revoked the order.

sentences.zh: 璟謝曰：「陛下向以怒責之，以臣言免之，是過歸於上而恩在下。

translations.literal: Jing apologized and said: "Your Majesty just now in anger punished them; because of my words you pardon them—this is fault returning above and grace falling below.
translations.idiomatic: Jing added, "Your anger blamed them; my plea saved them—the fault looks yours, the mercy mine.

sentences.zh: 姑聽待罪於朝，然後詔還其職，進退得矣。」

translations.literal: For the moment let them await punishment at court; only then issue an edict restoring their posts—advance and retreat would then be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Better let them stand guilty at court, then restore them properly—propriety would be preserved."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 累封廣平郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 廣人為璟立遺愛頌，璟上言：「頌所以傳德載功也。

translations.literal: The people of Guang erected for Jing a stele of enduring affection; Jing memorialized: "A eulogy is what transmits virtue and records achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou erected a laudatory stele; Jing wrote, "Praise exists to record true merit.

sentences.zh: 臣之治不足紀，廣人以臣當國，故為溢辭，徒成諂諛者。

translations.literal: My governance is insufficient to be recorded; the people of Guang, because I am in the national government, therefore made inflated words—it only completes flattery.
translations.idiomatic: I have done little worth praising; they exaggerated because I serve at court—that is mere flattery.

sentences.zh: 欲厘正之，請自臣始。」

translations.literal: Wishing to correct this, please begin with me."
translations.idiomatic: Stop it with me first."

sentences.zh: 有詔許停。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it to be halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor allowed the stele to be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗命璟與蘇頲制皇子名與公主號，遂差次所封，且詔別擇一美稱及佳邑封上。

translations.literal: The Emperor once ordered Jing and Su Ting to compose the imperial sons' names and the princesses' styles; they then ranked the enfeoffments in order, and an edict further ordered separately choosing one fine style and an excellent fief to ennoble the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Jing and Su Ting name the princes and princesses, rank their titles, and pick special epithets and rich fiefs for the eldest.

sentences.zh: 璟奏言：「七子均養，詩人所稱。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized: "The seven sons equally nourished is what the Odes praise.
translations.idiomatic: Jing argued, "The Book of Odes praises raising seven sons alike.

sentences.zh: 今若同等別封，或母寵子愛，恐傷跂鳩之平。

translations.literal: If now we enfeoff with separate ranks, or one mother is favored and one son loved, I fear it will injure the even balance of the perched dove.
translations.idiomatic: Unequal enfeoffments or a favorite queen's son would upset the dove's fair perch—the Odes' warning against favoritism.

sentences.zh: 昔袁盎引卻慎夫人席，文帝納之，夫人亦不為嫌，以其得長久計也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yuan Ang moved back Lady Shen's seat and Emperor Wen accepted it; the lady also was not resentful, because it was a plan for long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang once made Emperor Wen demote Lady Shen's seat; the emperor agreed, and the lady did not resent it, for the sake of lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢別封。」

translations.literal: Your servant dare not enfeoff separately."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept separate honors for the eldest."

sentences.zh: 帝歎重其賢。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed and valued his worth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at his integrity.

sentences.zh: 皇后父王仁籞卒，將葬，用昭成皇后家竇孝諶故事，墳高五丈一尺。

translations.literal: The empress's father Wang Renyue died; he was to be buried using the precedent of Empress Zhaocheng's family Dou Xiaochen—a mound five zhang one chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Wang Renyue died; the court proposed a tomb as high as Dou Xiaochen's for Empress Zhaocheng—five zhang one chi.

sentences.zh: 璟等請如著令，帝已然可，明日，復詔如孝諶者。

translations.literal: Jing and the others requested according to the written statutes; the Emperor already assented, but the next day again decreed as with Xiaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cited the statutes; the emperor agreed, then reversed himself to follow Xiaochen's precedent.

sentences.zh: 璟還詔曰：「儉，德之恭；

translations.literal: Jing returned the edict saying: "Frugality is the respect of virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Jing remonstrated: "Frugality is the crown of virtue;

sentences.zh: 侈，惡之大也。

translations.literal: extravagance is the greatest of evils.
translations.idiomatic: waste is the root of evil.

sentences.zh: 僭禮厚葬，前世所誡，故古墓而不墳。

translations.literal: Overstepping ritual with a thick burial is what past ages warned against; therefore ancient tombs were without mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant tombs broke ritual in every dynasty—hence the ancients buried without barrows.

sentences.zh: 人子於哀迷則未遑以禮自製，故聖人制齊、斬、緦、免，衣衾棺槨，各有度數。

translations.literal: When a son is lost in grief he has no leisure to restrain himself by ritual; therefore the sages established qi, zhan, si, and mian [mourning grades], with garments, covers, coffins, and outer cases—each with fixed measures.
translations.idiomatic: A grieving son cannot always govern himself by ritual; the sages therefore fixed mourning grades from deepest to lightest and set measures for shrouds, coffins, and outer cases.

sentences.zh: 雖有賢者，斷其私懷。

translations.literal: Even if there is a worthy man, [ritual] cuts off his private feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Even the wise must yield private sorrow to prescribed ritual.

sentences.zh: 眾皆務奢，獨能以儉，所謂至德要道者。

translations.literal: When all pursue extravagance, alone able to be frugal—this is what is called the utmost virtue and essential way.
translations.idiomatic: When everyone pursues display, to stand alone in thrift is the highest virtue and the heart of the Way.

sentences.zh: 中宮若謂孝諶逾制，初無非者，一切之令固不足以法。

translations.literal: If the inner palace says Xiaochen overstepped the statutes, at first there was no fault; a blanket order in any case is not enough to serve as law.
translations.idiomatic: If the empress argues that Xiaochen exceeded the rules, that was no fault in itself—and a blanket edict is no proper precedent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時嫁長樂公主，魏徵謂不可加長公主，太宗欣納，而文德皇后降使厚謝。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, when the Princess of Changle was married, Wei Zheng said one must not add to the Princess of Changle; Taizong gladly accepted, and Empress Wende sent envoys with generous thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At Princess Changle's wedding in the Zhenguan era, Wei Zheng warned against extra honors; Taizong agreed, and Empress Wende sent envoys to thank him warmly.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人追王其父，擅作，酆陵，而禍不旋踵。

translations.literal: Empress Wei the commoner ennobled her father posthumously, presumptuously made a Feng tomb, and calamity followed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei posthumously crowned her father and presumptuously built the Feng mound, ruin came almost at once.

sentences.zh: 國家知人情無窮，故為制度，不因人以搖動，不變法以愛憎。

translations.literal: The state knows human feelings are endless, therefore makes institutions, does not shift them for persons, does not change law for likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: The state knows desire has no limit, so it fixes institutions—neither bent by favoritism nor altered for private love or hate.

sentences.zh: 比來人間競務靡葬，今以後父重戚，不憂乏用，高塚大寢，不畏無人，百事官給，一朝可就，而區區屢聞者，欲成朝廷之政、中宮之美爾。

translations.literal: Recently the world competes in lavish burial; now as a queen's father and heavy in-law kin, not worried about shortage of goods, high mound and great tomb chamber, not fearing lack of men, a hundred affairs supplied by the office, completed in one morning—yet this trifling matter is heard again and again because one wishes to accomplish the court's governance and the inner palace's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Lavish funerals have become a contest; as the empress's father you need not fear want—a tall mound, a grand vault, labor and supplies from the state, all done in a day. We press this small point only to uphold public order and the empress's good name.

sentences.zh: 儻中宮情不可奪，請准令一品陪陵，墳四丈，差合所宜。」

translations.literal: If the inner palace's feeling cannot be overborne, I request approving the statute for a first-rank consort at the imperial tomb, a mound four zhang—roughly fitting what is proper."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cannot sway the empress, permit at least a first-rank consort's tomb by the mausoleum—four zhang high, which is near the proper measure."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕常欲正身紀綱天下，于後容有私邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have always wished to correct my person and bring order to the realm under Heaven; could there afterward be private partiality?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I mean to discipline myself and the realm—would I afterward allow private bias?

sentences.zh: 然人所難言，公等乃能之。」

translations.literal: Yet what men find hard to speak, you gentlemen were able to do."
translations.idiomatic: Yet what others dread to say, you dared speak plain."

sentences.zh: 即可其奏。

translations.literal: He at once approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He approved the memorial at once.

sentences.zh: 又遣使賚彩絹四百匹。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys bearing four hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys with four hundred bolts of colored silk as a gift.

sentences.zh: 會日食，帝素服俟變，錄囚多所貸遣，賑恤災患，罷不急之務。

translations.literal: There coincided a solar eclipse; the Emperor wore plain dress awaiting the change, recorded prisoners and pardoned many, relieved disaster victims, and suspended non-urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse fell; the emperor wore mourning white, awaited the omen's passage, pardoned many prisoners, aided disaster victims, and set aside nonessential business.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「陛下降德音，恤人隱，末宥輕系，惟流、死不免，此古所以慎赦也。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Your Majesty has issued a virtuous decree, comforted men's hidden distress, pardoned at the end light bonds—all except exile and death untouched; this is why antiquity was cautious about amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Your merciful edict comforts the afflicted and pardons petty offenders—only exile and capital crimes remain—which is why the ancients treated amnesty with care.

sentences.zh: 恐議者直以月蝕修刑，日蝕修德，或言分野之變，冀有揣合。

translations.literal: I fear counsellors will simply take lunar eclipse as cultivating punishment, solar eclipse as cultivating virtue, or speak of territorial correspondence, hoping for a match.
translations.idiomatic: I fear courtiers will say eclipses demand ritual reform—or match them to provincial portents and call that enough.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂君子道長，小人道銷。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the gentleman's way grows long, the petty man's way fades.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman's way should lengthen and the small man's way shorten.

sentences.zh: 止女謁，放讒夫，此所謂修德也。

translations.literal: Stopping women's access, releasing slanderers—this is what is called cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Bar palace intrigues and dismiss flatterers—that is true cultivation of virtue.

sentences.zh: 囹圄不擾，兵甲不瀆，官不苛治，軍不輕進，此所謂修刑也。

translations.literal: Prisons undisturbed, arms not profaned, officials not harsh in governance, armies not lightly advancing—this is what is called cultivating punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet the jails, keep arms holy, forbid harsh magistrates and rash campaigns—that is true cultivation of punishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下常以為念，雖有虧食，將轉而為福，又何患乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty should constantly keep this in mind; though there be a loss of nourishment [eclipse], it will turn into blessing—what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Hold to this and even a bite of heaven's food lost to shadow may become blessing—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 且君子恥言浮於行，願勸天以誠，無事空文。」

translations.literal: Moreover the gentleman is ashamed when words float above deeds; I wish to admonish Heaven with sincerity, not empty texts in vain."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman hates words that outrun deeds—urge sincerity upon heaven, not empty proclamations."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 後以開府儀同三司罷政事。

translations.literal: Later he was made Chief Director of the Palace with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes and removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Director of the Palace with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and left the ministry.

sentences.zh: 京兆人權梁山謀逆，敕河南尹王怡馳傳往按。

translations.literal: Quan Liangshan of Jingzhao plotted rebellion; an edict ordered Wang Yi, Intendant of Henan, to ride posthorses and go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Liangshan of Jingzhao plotted treason; the court ordered Henan Intendant Wang Yi to investigate by relay post.

sentences.zh: 牢械充滿，久未決，乃命璟為京留守，覆其獄。

translations.literal: Cells and shackles were full; long without verdict—then Jing was ordered as Capital Guardian to review the case.
translations.idiomatic: The jails overflowed and the case dragged on until Jing was named Capital Guardian to retry it.

sentences.zh: 初，梁山詭稱婚集，多假貸，吏欲並坐貸人。

translations.literal: At first Liangshan had falsely claimed a wedding gathering and borrowed much; clerks wished to punish lenders together.
translations.idiomatic: Liangshan had pretended a wedding feast to borrow widely; officials wanted every lender punished with him.

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「婚禮借索大同，而狂謀率然，非所防億。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Wedding rites and borrowing are much the same in custom, yet mad plotting arose suddenly—not what one could guard against in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Wedding loans are common custom, but his treason was sudden—no one could foresee it.

sentences.zh: 使知而不假，是與為反。

translations.literal: To say that if one knew one must not lend—that is to ally with rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: To punish lenders for knowing would imply they should have refused—and that would brand refusal as aiding the rebel.

sentences.zh: 貸者弗知，何罪之雲？」

translations.literal: The lenders did not know—what crime is spoken of?"
translations.idiomatic: The lenders knew nothing—what crime have they?"

sentences.zh: 平縱數百人。

translations.literal: He released several hundred at once.
translations.idiomatic: He freed several hundred.

sentences.zh: 十二年，東巡泰山，璟復為留守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he toured east to Mount Tai; Jing again served as guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve the emperor toured Mount Tai eastward; Jing again held the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝將發，謂曰：「卿，國元老，別方歷時，宜有嘉謀以遺朕。」

translations.literal: As the Emperor was about to depart, he said to him: "You, sir, are the state's elder, long apart in another region—there should be fine counsel to bequeath to Us."
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he said, "You are the state's elder, long away from court—leave me counsel worth keeping."

sentences.zh: 璟因一二極言。

translations.literal: Jing accordingly spoke one or two points to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Jing spoke bluntly on one or two points.

sentences.zh: 手制答曰：「所進當書之坐右，出入觀省，以誡終身。」

translations.literal: By autograph he replied: "What you presented should be written at my right hand; going out and in I shall look upon it to warn myself for life."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote back: "I shall copy what you offered at my right hand and read it going and coming, to guide me for life."

sentences.zh: 賜賚優渥，進兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Gifts were generous; he was advanced to concurrent Minister of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He received rich rewards and was promoted to concurrent Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十七年。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 為尚書右丞相，而張說為左丞相，源乾曜為太子少傅，同日拜。

translations.literal: He was made Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, while Zhang Yue was Left Chancellor and Yuan Qianyao Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent—they were appointed the same day.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Chancellor; Zhang Yue became Left Chancellor and Yuan Qianyao Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince—all appointed the same day.

sentences.zh: 有詔太官設饌，太常奏樂，會百官尚書省東堂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Grand Provisioner to set a feast, the Grand Director of Music to perform, and all officials to meet in the east hall of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a state banquet with music and gathered the officials in the east hall of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 帝賦三傑詩，自寫以賜。

translations.literal: The Emperor composed a poem on the Three Heroes and wrote it himself to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a poem on the three worthies and copied it himself as a gift.

sentences.zh: 二十年，請致仕，許之，仍賜全祿。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he requested retirement; it was granted, and he was still given full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty he asked to retire; the emperor agreed and granted full salary.

sentences.zh: 退居洛。

translations.literal: He retired to dwell in Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 乘輿東幸，璟謁道左。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured east, Jing met him at the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled east, Jing met him by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 詔榮王勞問，別遣使賜藥餌。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Rong to console him; separately envoys were sent with medicines.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Prince Rong to inquire after him and sent medicines by a separate envoy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年卒，年七十五，贈太尉，諡文貞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died, age seventy-five; posthumously made Grand Marshal, posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year twenty-five at seventy-five, was posthumously made Grand Marshal, and honored as Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 璟風度凝遠，人莫涯其量。

translations.literal: Jing's bearing was settled and distant; men could not fathom his measure.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's manner was remote and grave; none could plumb his depths.

sentences.zh: 始，自廣州入朝，帝遣內侍楊思勖驛迓之。

translations.literal: At first, coming to court from Guangzhou, the Emperor sent the inner attendant Yang Sixun by post to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first came from Guangzhou, the emperor sent the eunuch Yang Sixun by relay to meet him.

sentences.zh: 未嘗交一言。

translations.literal: [They] never exchanged a single word.
translations.idiomatic: They never exchanged a word.

sentences.zh: 思勖自以將軍貴幸，訴之帝，帝益嗟重。

translations.literal: Sixun, taking himself a general favored by fortune, complained to the Emperor; the Emperor all the more sighed and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun, proud of his rank and favor, complained; the emperor valued Jing all the more.

sentences.zh: 璟為宰相，務清政刑，使官人皆任職。

translations.literal: When Jing was chancellor he devoted himself to clarifying government and punishment, making every official fulfill his duty.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he cleared law and administration until every officer did his proper work.

sentences.zh: 聖曆後，突厥默啜負其強，數窺邊，侵九姓拔曳固，負勝輕出，為其狙擊斬之，入蕃使郝靈亻傳其首京師。

translations.literal: After the Shengli reign, the Türk Moqi chou relied on his strength, often spied at the border, invaded the Nine Surnames Bayegu; trusting victory he rode out lightly and was ambushed and beheaded; the envoy to the barbarians Hao Lingjian conveyed his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shengli era Moqi chou of the Turks, counting on strength, raided the frontier and attacked the Bayegu of the Nine Surnames; emboldened by victory he rode out carelessly, was ambushed and killed, and frontier envoy Hao Lingjian brought his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 靈佺自謂還必厚見賞。

translations.literal: Lingqian considered that on returning he would surely receive rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqian expected a lavish reward on his return.

sentences.zh: 璟顧天子方少，恐後幹寵蹈利者誇威武，為國生事，故抑之，逾年，才授右武衛郎將，靈佺恚憤不食死。

translations.literal: Jing, considering the Son of Heaven was still young, feared that later those who sought favor and pursued profit would boast martial might and create affairs for the state—therefore he restrained him; after more than a year he was only made Colonel of the Right Wuwei Guard; Lingqian, embittered, refused food and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing saw the emperor still young and feared future courtiers would boast of frontier glory and stir trouble—so he held back the reward; only after a year was Lingqian made colonel in the Right Wuwei Guard; embittered, he starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞後為相，閱堂案，見其危言切議，未嘗不失聲歎息。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen later became chancellor; reviewing desk dossiers, whenever he saw Jing's stern words and sharp counsel he never failed to sigh aloud.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiazhen later became chancellor, he read Jing's memorials of grave warning and always sighed aloud.

sentences.zh: 六子：升、尚、渾、恕、華、衡。

translations.literal: Six sons: Sheng, Shang, Hun, Shu, Hua, and Heng.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Sheng, Shang, Hun, Shu, Hua, and Heng.

sentences.zh: 子 升升，太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Son Sheng Sheng, Vice Minister of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng rose to Vice Minister of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 尚，漢東太守。

translations.literal: Shang, Administrator of Handong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang became Administrator of Handong.

sentences.zh: 子 渾渾，與李林甫善，曆諫議大夫、平原太守、御史中丞、東京採訪使。

translations.literal: Son Hun Hun, friendly with Li Linfu, passed through Remonstrating Censor, Administrator of Pingyuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hun, close to Li Linfu, served as Remonstrating Censor, Administrator of Pingyuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Eastern Capital commissioner.

sentences.zh: 在平原，暴斂求進，至重取民一年庸、租。

translations.literal: In Pingyuan he violently levied to seek advancement, even doubly taking from the people one year's corvée and land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In Pingyuan he extorted for promotion, even taking a double year's corvée and grain tax from the people.

sentences.zh: 使東畿，薛稷甥女鄭寡而美，渾使南尉楊朝宗聘而己納之，薦朝宗為赤尉。

translations.literal: Sent to the eastern capital region, Zheng—the niece by marriage of Xue Ji, widowed and beautiful—Hun had the southern bailiff Yang Chaozong court her and took her himself, then recommended Chaozong as red-uniform bailiff.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner in the eastern capital he saw Zheng, Xue Ji's widowed niece, famed for her beauty; Hun had southern bailiff Yang Chaozong court her but took her himself, then made Chaozong a bailiff of the red-uniform guard.

sentences.zh: 恕，以都官郎中為劍南採訪判官，數貪縱不法，陰養刺客。

translations.literal: Shu, as Director in the Department of Justice acting as judicial aide to the Sichuan commissioner, repeatedly was greedy and licentious beyond law, secretly keeping assassins.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, as aide to the Sichuan commissioner, repeatedly stole and broke the law and secretly kept assassins.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，渾、恕、尚並以贓敗，渾流高要，恕流海康，尚貶臨海長史。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era Hun, Shu, and Shang all fell to bribery; Hun was banished to Gaoyao, Shu to Haikang, Shang demoted to Chief of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Hun, Shu, and Shang were ruined by graft—Hun exiled to Gaoyao, Shu to Haikang, Shang demoted chief of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 華、衡亦皆坐貪得罪。

translations.literal: Hua and Heng also all sat because of greed and received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hua and Heng likewise fell for greed.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，渾起為太子諭德。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era Hun was raised to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangde era Hun was recalled as mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 物議穢薄之，流死江嶺。

translations.literal: Public opinion despised him; exiled, he died on the river ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion reviled him; he died in exile on the southern rivers.

sentences.zh: 昆弟皆荒飲俳嬉，而衡最險悖，廣平之風衰焉。

translations.literal: The brothers all drank wildly and played with performers; Heng was most dangerous and perverse—the Guangping family's style decayed.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers all drank and caroused with actors; Heng was the worst—the Guangping name withered.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：姚崇以十事要說天子而後輔政，顧不偉哉，而舊史不傳。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Yao Chong used ten essentials to persuade the Son of Heaven and afterward aided government—how is that not splendid! Yet the old histories do not record it.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: Yao Chong laid out ten essentials before he took office—magnificent, yet the old histories omit it.

sentences.zh: 觀開元初皆已施行，信不誣已。

translations.literal: Observing the early Kaiyuan, all were already carried out—truly not false.
translations.idiomatic: By early Kaiyuan his program was already in force—no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 宋璟剛正又過於崇，玄宗素所尊憚，常屈意聽納。

translations.literal: Song Jing was stern and upright and even surpassed Chong; Xuanzong from of old revered and feared him, often bending his intent to listen and accept.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing was more rigid than Chong; Xuanzong had long revered him and often bent his will to heed him.

sentences.zh: 故唐史臣稱崇善應變以成天下之務，璟善守文以持天下之正。

translations.literal: Therefore the Tang historiographer says Chong excelled at adapting to change to accomplish the realm's tasks, Jing excelled at guarding the written tradition to hold the realm's rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Tang historians say Chong adapted to finish the work of empire, Jing guarded the statutes to hold its rectitude.

sentences.zh: 二人道不同，同歸於治，此天所以佐唐使中興也。

translations.literal: The two men's ways differed yet alike returned to good order—this is how Heaven aided Tang to bring about restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Different paths, one peace—Heaven's way of helping Tang to its revival.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 崇勸天子不求邊功，璟不肯賞邊臣，而天寶之亂，卒蹈其害，可謂先見矣。

translations.literal: Chong urged the Son of Heaven not to seek frontier merit; Jing refused to reward frontier ministers—yet the Tianbao turmoil in the end trampled into that harm; it may be called foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Chong warned the emperor against frontier glory; Jing refused to reward border generals—the Tianbao catastrophe fulfilled both warnings: foresight indeed.

sentences.zh: 然唐三百年，輔弼者不為少，獨前稱房、杜，後稱姚、宋，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet in Tang's three hundred years, those who aided and restrained were not few; alone before they praise Fang and Du, after they praise Yao and Song—why?
translations.idiomatic: In three hundred years of Tang, helpers were many—yet only Fang and Du in the early reign, Yao and Song later: why?

sentences.zh: 君臣之遇合，蓋難矣夫！

translations.literal: The meeting and joining of ruler and minister—how difficult indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The meeting of ruler and minister is rare indeed!
